title: Commercial Lease Negotiation: Ten Preparation Steps for NSW Businesses
metaTitle: Commercial Lease Negotiation Preparation NSW | YOS
metaDescription: Prepare a commercial lease negotiation with a business brief, comparable costs, clear assumptions and adviser questions. Newcastle-based tenant-side support across NSW.
excerpt: Prepare the facts and decisions behind a lease negotiation. These ten steps help organise your brief, commercial comparisons and adviser inputs without assuming a guaranteed incentive or saving.
author: Joe Kelley
body:
## How should a business prepare for lease negotiation?

Define what the premises must do, identify the actual dates and compare the proposed commercial terms on a consistent basis. Preparation helps make trade-offs visible; it does not guarantee savings, rent-free periods, contributions or acceptance of a proposed clause.

This guide is a commercial preparation checklist for NSW businesses. Your solicitor advises on legal terms and documentation. YOS's tenant-side workstream and fees are agreed before engagement.

## 1. Confirm the dates and decision owners

Gather the lease or proposed terms and ask your solicitor to confirm relevant dates and requirements. Identify who can approve commercial instructions. Do not use a universal 12-month or 60-day rule to determine the options available.

**Helpful tip:** mark unverified dates as questions and assign someone to resolve each one.

[Organise confirmed lease dates](/tools/critical-dates)

## 2. Write the business brief

Record activities, peak attendance, access, location, space and growth assumptions. Separate essentials from preferences before comparing listings or renewal proposals.

**Helpful tip:** use the same brief when assessing the current site and alternatives.

[Prepare a Newcastle tenant representation brief](/blog/tenant-representation-brief-newcastle)

## 3. Check the evidence behind comparisons

Identify the date, property characteristics and limitations of any market evidence. Distinguish advertised asking terms from verified transaction information. Do not assume every comparable includes the same incentives or works.

**Helpful tip:** record missing information beside each comparison rather than filling gaps with an unsupported market average.

## 4. Compare the full commercial proposal

Record rent, available outgoings information, lease length, proposed review arrangements and the assumptions behind each offer. Identify the GST basis and keep one-off transition costs visible.

**Helpful tip:** compare consistent time periods and inclusions before judging the totals.

[Use the lease comparison tool](/resources/lease-comparison)

## 5. Treat incentives as proposed terms

Ask what is offered, its conditions, timing and how it interacts with the other costs. Do not assume an incentive is standard or include an unconfirmed contribution in an approved budget.

**Helpful tip:** distinguish requested, offered and documented terms in the comparison register.

## 6. Understand review assumptions

Ask your solicitor to explain the proposed rent-review wording and conditions, then model commercial scenarios using clearly labelled assumptions. Have the effect of any floor, cap or other mechanism assessed rather than treating a label as a benefit.

**Helpful tip:** show which future inputs remain uncertain instead of presenting a forecast as a fixed payment schedule.

## 7. Clarify end-of-lease questions

Gather condition records, plans and relevant amendments. Ask your solicitor to identify the obligations that need clarification before seeking a scoped estimate for any work.

**Helpful tip:** separate the interpretation of a lease obligation from the contractor's estimate for a specified job.

[Prepare a make-good scope and budget](/blog/make-good-obligations-commercial-lease-cost)

## 8. Connect premises and workplace delivery

Assess the likely layout, building constraints, landlord inputs, consultant requirements, furniture and technology changes. Record the steps needed before the business can operate.

**Helpful tip:** test the required operating date against project dependencies before assuming an available space is ready to use.

[Explore client-side FitOut project management](/office-fitout)

## 9. Discuss future business changes

Explain possible growth, downsizing, sale or relocation plans to your advisers. Ask your solicitor about proposed flexibility provisions and their conditions. Availability and legal effect depend on the actual transaction.

**Helpful tip:** frame the business need first, then obtain advice about the proposed wording.

## 10. Keep decisions and documents aligned

Maintain a register of proposed terms, open questions, agreed instructions and approval owners. Have your solicitor advise on documents and commitments before signing or relying on them.

**Helpful tip:** confirm the current revision and outstanding issues before a commercial approval is treated as final.

## Discuss the tenant-side workstream

YOS is Newcastle-based and provides tenant representation across NSW within the agreed service scope. We do not promise that benefits exceed fees or that particular terms will be secured.

[Explore Newcastle tenant representation](/tenant-rep/newcastle), [compare the packages](/tenant-rep#packages) or [send your leasing enquiry](#blog-contact-form).

For a current lease, [start a free Lease Health Check](/lease-health-check). Uploading your current lease is optional and further advisory work is scoped separately.

## Official guidance

The NSW Small Business Commissioner's preparation guidance encourages professional advice before committing to a lease.

The linked NSW retail leasing guidance should not be assumed to apply to every office or industrial lease. Ask your solicitor which requirements apply to your premises and transaction.

[NSW Small Business Commissioner: before you sign the lease](https://www.smallbusiness.nsw.gov.au/help/common-questions/before-you-sign-the-lease)
